chunks: What al-Shaykh—may Allah تعالى support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, all together, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Hamadhānī, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥannāṭ, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from al-Kalbī al-Nassābah: that he asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about nabīdh, so he said:

"Halal." He said: "We prepare nabīdh and then put into it the dregs and other than that." He said: "Fie, fie! That is the foul wine." He said: I said, "May I be your ransom, then which nabīdh do you mean?" He said: "The people of al-Madīnah complained to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about the change in the water and the corruption of their constitutions, so he ordered them to prepare nabīdh. A man would order his servant to prepare it for him, and he would take a handful of dates and throw it into the waterskin; from it was his drink and from it was his purification." I said: "How many dates were in the handful?" He said: "Whatever the hand could carry." I said: "One or two?" He said: "Sometimes it was one and sometimes it was two." I said: "How much did the waterskin hold?" He said: "Between forty and eighty, and more than that." I said: "By which ratls?" He said: "The ratls of the measure of Iraq."

Al-Shaykh—may Allah تعالى support him—said: Purification is also not permissible with waters that have been used in ghusl from impurities such as menstruation, istiḥāḍah, nifās, janābah, and washing the dead. There is no objection, however, to purification with water that has been used in washing the face and hands for the wudu of salat (prayer), and with water also used in washing pure bodies for a sunnah (prophetic tradition), such as the ghusl of Friday and the festivals. What is preferable is to seek pure waters that have not been used in performing an obligation or a sunnah, as we have explained. This is indicated by the fact that a person is required not to perform wudu except with what he is certain of its purity and is definite about the permissibility of salat (prayer) through its use. Water used in janābah is doubtful, so it is necessary that its use not be permissible. This is also indicated by...

key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: date-infused water; here, the lawful non-intoxicating preparation being discussed
key_terms.الْخَمْرَةُ: wine; here, the foul intoxicating form contrasted with lawful nabīdh
key_terms.الْمِيَاهِ الْمُسْتَعْمَلَةِ: used waters; water previously used in washing or purification
key_terms.طَهُورُهُ: his means of purification; water used for ritual cleansing

ai.seo_question: What kind of nabīdh is halal, and can used water be used again for ritual purification?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of nabīdh and clarifies that the permitted kind is a lightly infused drink made by placing a small amount of dates in water, not an intoxicating fermented beverage. The passage then shifts to a legal discussion on ritual purity, distinguishing between waters that may and may not be used for taharah after prior use.
